title: Few-shot Learning on AMS Circuits and Its Application to Parasitic Capacitance Prediction
problem: Predicting parasitic capacitance in analog/mixed-signal (AMS) circuit designs is critical for performance and power, but deep learning models require large labeled datasets that are scarce in IC design. Few-shot learning can exploit limited labeled data, but scalability and practical applicability remain open challenges.
motivation: AMS design iterations demand rapid parasitic extraction to close timing/power loops; training data scarcity limits supervised learning approaches, making few-shot transfer learning attractive.
method: CircuitGPS treats each circuit as a graph—a network where components are nodes and electrical coupling between them are connections. It uses a Transformer model (a machine learning system that learns patterns in networks) to analyze small neighborhoods of this graph. First, it learns to predict which component pairs are electrically coupled; then it learns how strong those couplings are. The system encodes structural information about each neighborhood, allowing it to learn from just a few labeled examples.
key_novelty: CircuitGPS learns to predict parasitic capacitance from few labeled examples by treating circuits as graphs with a Transformer model that captures structure, enabling it to work on new circuit designs without retraining.
contributions: CircuitGPS few-shot learning framework for parasitic capacitance prediction
Heterogeneous graph representation of AMS circuits with Transformer embeddings
Small-hop sampling and low-cost positional encoding for subgraph learning
≥20% accuracy gain on coupling existence, ≥0.067 MAE reduction on capacitance
Zero-shot scalability to diverse AMS circuit topologies

metrics.accuracy: 20% coupling existence accuracy gain; 0.067 MAE reduction
metrics.other: zero-shot generalization to diverse AMS designs

limitations: Evaluation on coupling capacitance only; scalability to other parasitics (resistance, inductance) and sub-7nm FinFET designs not discussed.
primary_theme: few-shot graph learning for scalable parasitic prediction in AMS circuits
